description: Trigger tests and structural assertions for the Playing to Win Claude Skill. Each eval verifies that the skill activates on a realistic operator prompt and produces the required 12-section output across four phases.

evals.label: explicit-framework-name
evals.prompt: Build me a Playing to Win framework around my new flat-fee bookkeeping service for Shopify DTC brands.

evals.label: abbreviation-trigger
evals.prompt: Run a P2W cascade on this offer: a $99/month newsletter for solo founders.

evals.label: pressure-test-trigger
evals.prompt: Pressure-test this idea: an AI tool that writes personalized birthday cards for executives.

evals.label: red-team-trigger
evals.prompt: Red-team this strategy: I want to be the default AI advisor for Fortune 500 CROs.

evals.label: where-to-play-trigger
evals.prompt: Where should we play with our scholarship matching product?

evals.label: codebase-invocation
evals.prompt: Build me a Playing to Win framework around this project.
evals.context: Invoked inside an open codebase with README.md, package.json, and marketing copy.
expected_behaviors: Reads README and package.json before producing output
Quotes existing positioning copy verbatim in Step 2a Discovery
Labels claims as FACT, INFERENCE, ASSUMPTION, or SPECULATION

evals.label: strategy-file-written
evals.prompt: P2W cascade for Northwind Books. Save the output.

evals.label: should-not-trigger-generic-advice
evals.prompt: Give me general business advice for a new startup.
evals.rationale: The skill should NOT trigger on generic business advice requests. Triggers require explicit framework naming or pressure-test / red-team / where-to-play language.
